card.name: Waiting until a toxicity has resolved
card.fires_on: The word just after an adverse event or symptom in dose-hold instructions, mostly 'has' or 'have' before 'resolved'. It also fires on the event noun itself, such as toxicity or vomiting.

modes.label: Event then has resolved
modes.description: Auxiliary 'has/have' after a toxicity, bleeding or symptom noun in hold-then-resume instructions.
modes.example: Withhold nilotinib capsules until toxicity<< has>> resolved.

modes.label: Event noun before resolved
modes.description: The toxicity or symptom noun itself, right before 'has resolved'.
modes.example: Monitor until nausea or<< vomiting>> has resolved to Grade 2 or lower

modes.label: Other linking words in clinical context
modes.description: Scattered words after a clinical event, such as hospital before ization, or following and beyond.
modes.example: other interventions, including<< hospital>>ization, should be considered

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward a follow-on verb such as resolved, and away from admission-related words.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a dosing instruction where the text waits for a side effect to clear before resuming.
